Introduction

Globalization and Regionalism are two major phenomena influencing global trends. Both as a form of integration and differentiation among states, they characterize a form of reorganization of interstate relations, both formal and informal. Globalization is often understood as a phenomenon or a process characterized by increasing interconnectedness or interdependence—it is a supra-regional process bringing the world into one "global village". The economy, politics, and technology have been the driving forces of globalization. Regionalism, on the other hand, is conceived as a way of dealing with politico-economic, social, military, and security issues affecting states in common. Both developments continue to shape the nature of global politics, peace, and security through complex interplay involving convergence, divergence, and overlap.

👉

🌐 ግሎባላይዜሽን እና ሪጅናሊዝም (Globalization & Regionalism)፦
• ግሎባላይዜሽን (Globalization)፦ በሀገራት መካከል ያለውን ግንኙነትና ጥገኝነት (Interconnectedness & Interdependence) የሚጨምር፣ መላውን ዓለም ወደ አንድ "ዓለም አቀፍ መንደር" (Global Village) የሚቀይር ድበር ተሻጋሪ ሂደት ነው። ዋና ተሳታፊ ኃይሎቹ ኢኮኖሚ፣ ፖለቲካ እና ቴክኖሎጂ ናቸው።
• ሪጅናሊዝም (Regionalism)፦ በአንድ በኩል የተወሰኑ በጂኦግራፊ የተሳሰሩ ሀገራት በጋራ የሚጋፈጧቸውን የፖለቲካ፣ ኢኮኖሚ፣ ማህበራዊ እና የደህንነት/ወታደራዊ ጉዳዮች በጋራ ለመፍታት የሚፈጥሩት ቀጣናዊ ትስስር ነው።

4.1. Defining Globalization

Globalization can be defined as a multidimensional process characterized by four key interrelated features:

  1. Stretching of Social and Political Activities: Social and political activities are stretched across state (political) frontiers so that events, decisions, and activities in one part of the world come to have significance for individuals and communities in other distant parts of the world. Example: Wars and conflicts in developing countries directly increase the flow of asylum seekers and illegal migrants into developed countries.
  2. Intensification or Growing Magnitude of Interconnectedness: Interconnectedness is intensified across almost every aspect of social existence—ranging from the economic to the ecological, the spread of global health crises like HIV-AIDS, the intensification of world trade, to the proliferation and spread of different weapons.
  3. Accelerating Pace or Velocity of Global Interactions: The pace of global interactions and processes is rapidly accelerating as the evolution of worldwide systems of transport and communication increases the rapidity or velocity with which ideas, news, goods, information, capital, and technology move around the world.
  4. Deepening Enmeshment of the Local and Global: Local events come to have serious global consequences, and global events come to have direct local consequences, creating a growing collective awareness of the world as a shared social space—often referred to as globality or globalism.

Time-Space Compression and Deterritorialization: Although geography and distance still matter, globalization is synonymous with a process of time-space compression—meaning that in a shrinking world, events or actions no longer coincide strictly with the physical place in which they occur. Globalization embodies a process of deterritorialization, wherein social, political, and economic activities are increasingly stretched across the globe and are no longer organized solely according to territorial logic. For example, terrorists and transnational criminals operate simultaneously at local and global levels. Similarly, national economic space is no longer coterminous with national territorial space, as seen in many U.S. multinational companies maintaining their operational headquarters or production lines in Europe or Asia. Consequently, the traditional distinction between domestic and international, or "inside" and "outside" the state, breaks down.

📌
ግሎባላይዜሽን በ4 ዋና ዋና አምዶች/ባህሪያት የሚገለፅ ዘመነ-ብዙ (Multidimensional) ሂደት ነው፦
1. የእንቅስቃሴዎች መዘርጋት (Stretching of Activities)፦ በአንድ የዓለም ጥግ የሚፈጠር ክስተት በሌላው ጥግ ላይ ቀጥተኛ ተፅዕኖ ያሳድራል። ምሳሌ፦ በታዳጊ ሀገራት የሚነሱ ጦርነቶችና ግጭቶች ወደ በለፀጉ ሀገራት የሚሄዱ ስደተኞችና ጥገኝነት ጠያቂዎች (Asylum seekers) ቁጥር እንዲጨምር ያደርጋል።
2. የትስስር መጠን መጨመር (Intensification of Interconnectedness)፦ ከኢኮኖሚ እስከ ሥነ-ምህዳር፣ የኤችአይቪ/ኤድስ ስርጭት፣ የዓለም ንግድ እና የጦር መሳሪያዎች መስፋፋት በከፍተኛ ሁኔታ ተሳስረዋል።
3. የግንኙነት ፍጥነት መጨመር (Accelerating Velocity)፦ በትራንስፖርትና በኢንፎርሜሽን ቴክኖሎጂ እድገት ምክንያት መረጃዎች፣ ገንዘብ፣ እቃዎችና ሀሳቦች በከፍተኛ ፍጥነት ይዘዋወራሉ።
4. የሀገር ውስጥና የዓለም አቀፍ ክስተቶች መወዳጀት (Deepening Enmeshment / Globality)፦ የአካባቢ (Local) ክስተቶች የዓለም አቀፍ (Global) ውጤት ይኖራቸዋል፤ የዓለም አቀፍ ክስተቶችም በሀገር ውስጥ ሕይወት ላይ ቀጥተኛ ተፅዕኖ ያሳድራሉ።
• Time-Space Compression (የጊዜና ቦታ መኮማተር) እና Deterritorialization (ወሰን-አልባነት)፦ ርቀትና ጂኦግራፊ አሁንም ቢኖሩም፣ ዓለም በመኮማተሯ የተነሳ ድበርና የሀገር ወሰን የኢኮኖሚና ፖለቲካ ብቸኛ መወሰኛ መሆናቸው ቀርቷል። ምሳሌ፦ የሽብርተኞችና የዓለም አቀፍ ወንጀለኞች ድበር ተሻግረው መንቀሳቀሳቸው፣ እንዲሁም እንደ አሜሪካ ያሉ ኩባንያዎች ዋና መሥሪያ ቤታቸውን በአውሮፓ ማድረጋቸው የሀገር ውስጥ (Domestic) እና የዓለም አቀፍ (International) ልዩነት እንዲጠፋ አድርጎታል።

4.2. The Globalization Debates

Globalization is a contentious and highly debated issue in international relations. Scholars are divided into three major theoretical perspectives regarding its direction, nature, and political consequences for sovereign statehood: The Hyper-globalists, The Skeptics, and The Transformationalists.

4.2.1. The Hyper-globalists

For hyper-globalists, contemporary globalization defines a primary new epoch in human history in which traditional nation-states have become obsolete and powerless to regulate their national economies and borders. Key assertions include:

  • Economic over Political: Privileges the global market over the state. Economic globalization brings about the "de-nationalization" or "de-territorialization" of economies through transnational networks of production, trade, and finance.
  • States as Transmission Belts: National governments are relegated to little more than "transmission belts" for global capital or powerless institutions marginalized by regional and global governance mechanisms.
  • Winners and Losers (North-South Gap): Economic globalization creates a new pattern of winners and losers. It accentuates the South-North gap, creating a complex international division of labor that challenges traditional welfare states in supporting those disadvantaged by liberal market competition.
  • Global Uniform Culture: Imparts new liberal ideas and a culture of modernization, eroding traditional local cultures and establishing a new global order marked by uniform cultural values and ways of life.

👉

1️⃣ ሃይፐር-ግሎባሊስቶች ግሎባላይዜሽን የብሔራዊ ሀገራትን (Nation-states) ስልጣንና ጥቅም ያከሰመ፣ ሀገራት ኢኮኖሚያቸውንና ድበራቸውን የመቆጣጠር አቅማቸውን ያጡበት አዲስ የሰው ልጅ ታሪክ ምዕራፍ ነው ብለው ያምናሉ።
• ገበያ ከመንግሥት ይበልጣል፦ ገበያ (Market) ከመንግሥት (State) በላይ ሆኗል። ሀገራት የዓለም አቀፍ ካፒታል "ማስተላለፊያ ገመድ" (Transmission belts) ብቻ ሆነዋል።
• አሸናፊና ተሸናፊ (Winners & Losers)፦ በበለፀጉት (North) እና ታዳጊ (South) ሀገራት መካከል ያለውን ልዩነት በማስፋት አዲስ የሥራ ክፍፍል ፈጥሯል፤ የማህበራዊ ደህንነት (Welfare) መንግስታትን አቅም አዳክሟል።
• አንድ ወጥ ባህል (Uniform Culture)፦ የአካባቢ ነባር ባህሎችን በማጥፋት የዶላርና የነፃ ገበያ አስተሳሰብን መሰረት ያደረገ አንድ ወጥ የዓለም አቀፍ ባህል ይፈጥራል።

4.2.2. The Skeptics

Skeptics reject the hyper-globalist perspective as a myth, flawed, and politically naive. They argue that hyper-globalists fundamentally underestimate the enduring power of national governments to regulate economic activity:

  • Globalization vs. Internationalization: What is termed "globalization" is merely a heightened degree of internationalization or regionalization—a process deeply dependent on the regulatory power of states to enforce economic liberalism.
  • Regional Blocs over Global Village: Rejects the concept of a seamless "global village". Instead of a borderless world, the world economy is divided into distinct regional financial and trading blocs: the European Union (EU) in Europe, NAFTA in North America, and ASEAN in Asia.
  • Reinforcement of Inequality and Hierarchy: There is no true free flow of technology, capital, and finance at a global level; flows are concentrated within Western developed nations. Developing nations (Global South) remain integrated primarily as suppliers of primary agricultural commodities under unfavorable terms of trade, reinforcing existing North-South inequalities and structural hierarchies.

👉

2️⃣ ስኬፕቲክስ / ተጠራጣሪዎች (The Skeptics) የሃይፐር-ግሎባሊስቶችን እይታ "የተሳሳተ ተረት/ተስፋ" (Myth) ነው ብለው ውድቅ ያደርጋሉ። መንግስታት አሁንም ቢሆን የዓለም ኢኮኖሚን የመቆጣጠርና የመምራት ከፍተኛ ስልጣን አላቸው።
• ግሎባላይዜሽን ሳይሆን ሪጅናላይዜሽን ነው፦ መላው ዓለም አንድ መንደር ሆኗል የሚለውን አይቀበሉም። በዓለም ደረጃ ሳይሆን በክልል/ቀጠና ደረጃ የተዋቀሩ የንግድ ብሎኮች (Regional Trading Blocs) ነው ያሉት። ምሳሌ፦ EU በአውሮፓ፣ NAFTA በሰሜን አሜሪካ፣ ASEAN በእስያ።
• የቀጠለ የበላይነትና ኢ-ፍትሃዊነት፦ ነፃ የካፒታልና የቴክኖሎጂ ዝውውር የለም፤ በለፀጉት ሀገራት ታዳጊ ሀገራትን የግብርና ጥሬ እቃ ማቅረቢያ ብቻ በማድረግ የሰሜን-ደቡብ (North-South) ልዩነትና የኢኮኖሚ ጭቆና እንዲቀጥል አድርገዋል።

4.2.3. The Transformationalist

Central to the transformationalist perspective is the conviction that globalization is an unprecedented, critical driving force behind rapid social, political, and economic transformations reshaping contemporary societies and international politics:

  • Reconstitution of State Power: Rejects both the hyper-globalist "end of the sovereign state" claim and the skeptic "nothing much has changed" position. They assert that state sovereignty is not disappearing, but is being reconstituted, reengineered, and transformed.
  • Sovereignty as a Bargaining Resource: Traditional state power as absolute, indivisible, and territorially exclusive is displaced. Sovereignty today is best understood as a bargaining resource within complex transnational networks rather than a rigid territorial barrier.
  • Rise of Non-State Actors & Diffused Authority: Authority is no longer purely state-centric; it has become diffused upward (to international regulatory agencies), downward (to sub-national entities), and sideways (to Multinational Corporations [MNCs] and transnational social movements).

4.3. Globalization and Its Impacts on Africa

In its essential nature, globalization represents the compression of time and space, reducing the world into a "Global Village" or through "Villagization". Contemporary globalization is driven by financial flows, trade, transport, information technology, and the global diffusion of ideas, culture, and ideologies. However, it is also defined by the Americanization of the world, the propagation of a universal developmental paradigm, and the dominance of American unilateralism.

Driving Forces & US Hegemony

The Americanization of the world stems from an unprecedented gap between the United States and its rivals in military, economic, technological, and cultural domains. This converts into unequal American influence within international decision-making and major institutions such as the United Nations, Bretton Woods institutions (IMF and World Bank), and the WTO. The international system has transitioned from multipolar or bipolar configurations to an imperial system under American hegemony, enforcing the Washington Consensus—a universal model emphasizing market forces and liberal democracy without regard for the historical and cultural specificities of individual countries.

Specific Impacts on Africa

  • Cold War & Post-Cold War Trajectories: During the Cold War (1960s-1970s), superpowers supported authoritarian, one-party, or military regimes in Africa to maintain ideological blocs. With the end of the Cold War, strategic support was abruptly withdrawn, causing a decline in Africa's strategic importance and negotiating power, directly contributing to the rise of "failed states" over the last two decades.
  • Erosion of State Sovereignty & Anti-Developmentalism: Structural Adjustment Programs (SAPs) and policies imposed by the IMF, World Bank, and WTO stripped African governments of their capacity to determine domestic economic policies. Donors pushed stabilization and privatization over growth and poverty eradication, declaring the state "irrelevant" to development. Basic social welfare responsibilities were transferred to NGOs, eroding state legitimacy and authority.
  • Enclave Economies & Marginalization: Imposed economic specialization forced African nations into "enclave economies"—producing raw primary agricultural commodities for export with minimal domestic linkages. This stifled the emergence of an indigenous entrepreneurial class and reinforced social divisions along ethnicity, religion, race, and location.
  • Socio-Cultural & Brain Drain Consequences: Economic stagnation and marginalization triggered severe "brain drain" (loss of educated professionals). Cultural domination from outside eroded local cultural identities, while vulnerability among women, youth, and rural populations intensified.

4.4. Ethiopia in a Globalized World

Ethiopia was marginally integrated into the capitalist global system during the post-Cold War era. Following a 17-year interruption during the socialist Derg regime, Ethiopia re-entered the global capital framework post-1991. The processes of democratization and post-conflict state reconstruction coincided directly with the advent of contemporary globalization, leaving explicit marks on national policies, including the formulation of the FDRE Constitution.

Marginal Integration and the Cautious Developmental State

According to the late Prime Minister of FDRE, Meles Zenawi, Ethiopia's marginal integration into the global capitalist system—combined with the cautious developmental state political economy pursued by EPRDF—saved the country from being adversely affected by the onslaught of global capital and the 2008 global financial crisis that severely plagued Western market economies and fully integrated developing nations.

Collision of Paradigms & Multidimensional Impacts

  • Collision with Bretton Woods Institutions: The triumph of Western free market economy and liberal democracy created a head-on collision course between Ethiopia's defiant developmental state economic policy and the structural demands of Bretton Woods institutions (IMF and World Bank) and Western powers, impacting development aid and loan negotiations.
  • Positive Impact Opportunities: Despite challenges, strategic planning enabled Ethiopia to achieve remarkable economic transformation, benefiting from technological and knowledge transfer, foreign direct investment, and the free movement of ideas, finance, and people.
  • Negative Socio-Cultural & Political Impacts:
    • Opening historical doors to new religious and secular values affected traditional social solidarity, contributing to the rise of religious radicalism of various postures.
    • Western cultural values heavily eroded traditional practices in urban centers.
    • Glocalization dynamics (simultaneous global integration and local differentiation) fueled radical nationalism and ethnicity, exacerbating identity-based conflicts.
    • Human trafficking and illegal migration expanded rapidly.

Conclusion on Ethiopia: Overall, evidence indicates that Ethiopia has benefited significantly less from globalization than it has suffered from its negative influences.

4.5. Pros and Cons of Globalization

Globalization presents a complex matrix of merits (opportunities) and demerits (challenges) for contemporary international relations and sovereign states.

Merits (Pros / Positive Impacts)Demerits (Cons / Negative Impacts)
  • Expansion of democratic culture, human rights, and protection of minority and subaltern groups.
  • Scientific, medical, and ICT innovations drastically improving overall quality of life.
  • Agricultural technological expansion lifting millions of people out of absolute poverty.
  • Advancement of human security and safety standards globally.
  • Free movement of goods, services, people, ideas, expertise, knowledge, and technology strengthening international interdependence.
  • Emergence of global citizenship and global civil society.
  • Establishment of the Responsibility to Protect (R2P) vulnerable populations from human rights violations.
  • Rapid economic growth in several developing nations of the Global South.
  • Imposed by a global financial elite, widening the gap between the rich and the poor.
  • Western imperialism of ideas eroding the sovereignty and culture of non-Western nations.
  • Macroeconomic forces operating beyond the effective control of national governments and MNCs.
  • Global capital, IMF, and World Bank negatively dictating economic and political dynamics in poor nations.
  • Multiplication of climatic, environmental, and technological risks.
  • Threat to the continuity of non-Western age-old traditions and cultural values.
  • Globalization of risks: global terrorism, religious fundamentalism, proliferation of Small Arms and Light Weapons (SALWs), human and arms trafficking.
  • Triggering Glocalization (integration + local differentiation), leading to radical nationalism, ethnic politics, and identity conflicts.

⚖️ የግሎባላይዜሽን ጥቅሞችና ጉዳቶች (Pros and Cons of Globalization)፦
• ጥቅሞች (Pros)፦ የዲሞክራሲና ሰብአዊ መብቶች መስፋፋት፣ የቴክኖሎጂና ህክምና እድገት፣ የግብርና ቴክኖሎጂ ሚሊዮኖችን ከድህነት ማውጣቱ፣ የዕቃና እውቀት ነፃ ዝውውር፣ የዓለም አቀፍ ዜግነት (Global Citizenship) እና የጋራ ደህንነት (Responsibility to Protect) መፈጠር።
• ጉዳቶች (Cons)፦ በሀብታምና ድሃ መካከል ያለውን ልዩነት ማስፋቱ፣ የምዕራባውያን ባህላዊና ሀሳባዊ ኢምፔሪያሊዝም፣ የአካባቢ ጥበቃና የአየር ንብረት አደጋዎች መጨመር፣ የሽብርተኝነት፣ የሃይማኖት አክራሪነት፣ አነስተኛ የጦር መሳሪያዎች (SALWs) እና የሰዎች ህገ-ወጥ ዝውውር ድበር ተሻጋሪ መሆን፣ እንዲሁም Glocalization ያስከተለው የብሄርና የፖለቲካ ግጭቶች።
